transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Avery Chen (CTO, Solace), Miguel Torres (SRE), Hannah Park (Product), Samir Gupta (ML Eng)

Summary:
High-level POC scoping call focused on defining latency and throughput SLOs for a pilot using Redwood Dedicated/private deployment options. Main topics: TTFT vs TPOT definitions, p95/p99 targets, workload sizing (tokens/sec, concurrent reqs), benchmark plan (harness, synthetic vs replay), and timeline for a 4-week POC. Action items and next steps captured at the end. Transcript has occasional transcription noise (names, acronyms).

Topics:
- Definitions: TTFT (time to first token) vs TPOT (time per token or throughput per token)
- Desired SLO tiers: interactive vs batch workloads (p95/p99)
- Measurement methodology: synthetic microbenchmarks, replay of production traces, warm/cold cache differentiation
- Workload sizing: concurrency, median seq len, 95th token length, tokens/sec, KV cache hit rates
- Acceptance criteria and go/no-go for POC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: okay hi everybody, thanks for joining. um quick intros real fast then we can jump in. i'm jordan lee, AE at Redwood. priya is our se and she'll drive the perf side.
[00:08] Avery: hey all, avery here. thanks. we want to make sure this POC proves we can meet sub-200ms interactive latencies at scale, or at least know the tradeoffs.
[00:18] Priya: great, hey team. two quick clarifying q's before we define SLOs: are you mostly interactive chat flows or long-generation batch jobs?
[00:25] Hannah: mostly interactive chat for customer support, ~80% of traffic, and some summarization jobs that run as background batch.
[00:33] Miguel: plus a small high-throughput pipeline for embeddings on a schedule. but this call should focus on the chat SLOs.
[00:38] Jordan: perfect. so commonly we measure TTFT — time to first token — for perceived latency, and TPOT — time per token or tokens/sec — for throughput. we usually define p95 and p99 SLOs for each.
[00:50] Samir: quick q, are folks using TTFT to mean first byte or first token? we log first byte in our infra.
[00:55] Priya: yes, good point. we recommend instrumenting at the token emission boundary, so TTFT = time from request acceptance to first emitted token from the model. that avoids network proxy variance.
[01:07] Miguel: ok that helps. our current traces show average first byte at ~120ms but p99 spikes to ~550ms during peaks.
[01:15] Priya: yeah those peaks matter. for interactive chat you probably want p95 < 200ms and p99 < 400-500ms depending on acceptance. what's your tolerance?
[01:24] Avery: target p95 180ms, p99 450ms. if we hit p95 under 200 but p99 occasionally at 600, that's risky — we'd like clear mitigation.
[01:34] Jordan: noted. we should also agree TPOT or tokens/sec targets. for your use case what's the typical response lengths?
[01:40] Hannah: median response ~30 tokens, 95th ~120 tokens.
[01:44] Samir: concurrency wise, average QPS ~30 during business hours with short peaks to 120 qps in 10-minute windows for events.
[01:51] Priya: ok we need to size the POC to reproduce those peak windows — so target concurrency of 150 simulated clients with a token distribution matching your logs.
[02:00] Miguel: we can provide 1 week of logs. note some of those spikes correlate with batch jobs starting, so we'll mark those windows.
[02:07] Jordan: good — for measurement plan we usually run three tiers: cold-start profile, warm profile (after KV/prefix cache warmed), and steady-state sustained load for throughput.
[02:17] Priya: yes, and measurements: TTFT p95/p99 for first token, median and mean TPOT (ms/token) and tokens/sec overall, and end-to-end tail latency for full response generation. also track GPU util and queueing latencies.
[02:30] Samir: how do we measure TPOT in streaming models? we have partial chunks emitted.
[02:33] Priya: you can measure token inter-arrival time at the server emission point; average across tokens after the first N warm tokens to avoid model startup. we also report effective tokens/sec per GPU.
[02:45] Hannah: what's acceptable TPOT for our median 30-token responses?
[02:48] Priya: if TTFT is 180ms and TPOT is ~8-12ms/token steady, then a 30-token response median finishes in about 420ms total. that's inline with p95 goals.
[02:56] Miguel: and p99 will be dominated by queueing during spikes. can Redwood do autoscale or dedicated reserved pools?
[03:02] Jordan: yes — POC options: hosted with burst vs Dedicated reserved GPU pools. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and avoids noisy neighbors, and we can set autoscale policies for burst capacity.
[03:11] Samir: we'd prefer dedicated for guaranteed tails. cost is secondary in POC but we need to model unit economics.
[03:17] Jordan: understood. part of the POC deliverables: cost-per-1k-tokens at the chosen quantization/instance config.
[03:24] Priya: back to the measurement plan: we'll run replay tests with your real traces, and synthetic microbenchmarks to isolate model vs infra overhead. we'll capture TTFT with and without KV cache hits to show improvement.
[03:36] Miguel: note our prefix cache hit rate is about 45% for common dialogs; that matters.
[03:42] Priya: absolutely — we'll include hit-rate variation scenarios: 0%, 45%, 90% to show sensitivity.
[03:48] Hannah: what about p99 targets for long responses (95th token length 120)?
[03:52] Priya: for long tails we typically set p95 < 800ms and p99 < 1.5s for 120-token responses on Dedicated — but exact numbers depend on model size (7B vs 70B), quantization, and batch packing.
[04:05] Samir: prefer using a 13B-quantized model to start; cheaper but still acceptable quality. can Redwood recommend quant profiles?
[04:11] Jordan: yes, our Optimize team provides quantization profiles per model for the workload; we'll include recommended configs in the plan.
[04:17] Miguel: measurement cadence? how many runs to be statistically meaningful?
[04:20] Priya: we run 3 repeated steady-state runs of 30 minutes each for throughput and tail stability, plus 5 cold-start runs for startup behaviour. that gives us enough samples for p95/p99 estimation.
[04:31] Jordan: also capture resource metrics: GPU p99 util, memory, queue length, infra latency per hop. we'll provide a dashboard link with token-level breakdowns.
[04:39] Hannah: ok good. timeline for a 4-week POC?
[04:43] Jordan: suggested timeline: week 0 (this week) finalize scope and sign POC SOW; week 1 run basic microbenchmarks + baseline replay of 1 day; week 2 run full 1-week replay and peak window stress tests; week 3 tune config and run regression tests; week 4 wrap-up, handoff, and decision meeting.
[04:58] Miguel: we can commit to providing logs and a test account. need security review — SOC2 and SSO are required.
[05:04] Jordan: noted — we'll share SOC2 report and SAML/SCIM docs. we'll also provide a limited-data flow diagram for the POC.
[05:11] Samir: about measurement noise — network proxies add jitter. can we run initial tests within the same VPC or use private deployment?
[05:18] Priya: yes we can run Redwood Private in your VPC or a dedicated subnet to minimize network variance; that will give more accurate TTFT measurement.
[05:25] Hannah: any gotchas on metric definitions? we've seen different vendors report 'latency' differently.
[05:29] Priya: we'll provide a measurement spec doc that states precisely: TTFT = t_model_emit_first_token - t_request_received_by_inference_runtime; TPOT = average inter-token emission time measured at runtime; end-to-end = time until last token emitted + client-side render time (if measured). we'll also share the harness code for reproducibility.
[05:46] Avery: perfect. on acceptance criteria: primary gate is SLO meeting for interactive chat: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 500ms for median-size responses; plus throughput required to sustain 120 qps peaks with <10% request queuing.
[06:00] Samir: and secondary gate is cost per 1k tokens below our internal threshold — we expect Redwood to provide cost estimates for each config.
[06:08] Jordan: we will. additionally, we'll run quality checks on the sample prompt set to ensure quantization/config doesn't degrade output beyond your tolerance — we'll record difference metrics.
[06:17] Miguel: who owns the prompt set?
[06:19] Samir: i'll own that; i'll prepare top-50 prompts and label expected outputs.
[06:23] Jordan: great. last quick notes: we'll annotate each test with cache hit-rate, model size, quant settings, and instance shape.
[06:30] Priya: and provide step-by-step runbook so your SREs can reproduce locally.
[06:34] Hannah: sounds good. any legal/contract items for the SOW?
[06:37] Jordan: legal will use a standard POC SOW with limited liability and data handling addendum; we'll attach SOC2 and DPA.
[06:45] Avery: ok thanks, that's clear.
[06:47] Jordan: cool — recap next steps: jordan send pricing and plan, priya share harness, solace provide logs and prompt set, schedule deep dive week of 7/19.
[06:56] Miguel: great, thanks all.
[07:00] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links. bye.

End of transcript.
